title: Weyl quantization, Wigner functions and finite-time classical limits

items.title: Schwartz Weyl quantization and Wigner distributions
items.statement:
Let $d\geq1$, let $0<\epsilon$ be a dimensionless parameter, and use the Schwartz space $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ of [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]. For $a\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{2d})$, define the Weyl quantization on $u\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ by

$$ (\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(a)u)(x):=(2\pi\epsilon)^{-d}\int_{\mathbb R^d}\int_{\mathbb R^d} e^{i(x-y)\cdot\xi/\epsilon}a\!\left(\frac{x+y}{2},\xi\right)u(y)\,d\xi\,dy . $$

The integral is absolutely convergent for each fixed $x$, since its integrand is Schwartz in $(y,\xi)$. The Wigner integral below is absolutely convergent for each $(x,\xi)$ for the same reason.

For $u\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ satisfying
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}|u(x)|^2\,dx=1,$$
define its Wigner distribution by

$$ W_\epsilon[u](x,\xi):=(2\pi\epsilon)^{-d}\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-iy\cdot\xi/\epsilon}u(x+y/2)\overline{u(x-y/2)}\,dy . $$

Use the inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\int f(x)\overline{g(x)}\,dx$, linear in its first argument ([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]). Define the scaled Fourier transform on $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ by

$$ (\mathcal F_\epsilon u)(\xi):=(2\pi\epsilon)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-ix\cdot\xi/\epsilon}u(x)\,dx . $$

For the coordinate and momentum observables define $Q_j u=x_j u$ and $P_j u=-i\epsilon\partial_{x_j}u$ on $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$. Applying the real product rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) to the real and imaginary components, with the componentwise derivative convention of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]], gives
$$ Q_jP_ku=-i\epsilon x_j\partial_{x_k}u,\qquad P_kQ_ju=-i\epsilon(\delta_{jk}u+x_j\partial_{x_k}u),\qquad [Q_j,P_k]u:=Q_jP_ku-P_kQ_ju=i\epsilon\delta_{jk}u. $$
This fixes the Poisson and Moyal signs used on this page.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $\epsilon>0$, and define $\mathcal F_\epsilon$ on $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ by [[def-nrqmx-weyl-symbol-wigner]]. It extends uniquely to a unitary operator on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$.

items.title: Square-integrable kernel bound for Schwartz Weyl quantization
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\geq1$, $\epsilon>0$, and $a\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{2d})$. The kernel of $\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(a)$ is

$$ K_\epsilon(x,y):=(2\pi\epsilon)^{-d}\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{i(x-y)\cdot\xi/\epsilon}a\!\left(\frac{x+y}{2},\xi\right)\,d\xi . $$

It belongs to $L^2(\mathbb R^{2d})$ and satisfies

$$ \|K_\epsilon\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^{2d})}=(2\pi\epsilon)^{-d/2}\|a\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^{2d})}. $$

The kernel integral defines a bounded operator on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$ that agrees with the Schwartz-space definition of $\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(a)$, and its operator norm is at most the displayed kernel norm. This estimate is finite for each $\epsilon>0$ but is not uniform as $\epsilon\downarrow0$.

items.title: Wigner pairing and marginals
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\geq1$, $\epsilon>0$, $a\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{2d})$, and $u\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ satisfy $\|u\|_2=1$. With the definitions of [def-nrqmx-weyl-symbol-wigner], the Wigner distribution $W_\epsilon[u]$ is real and integrable, and

$$ \langle\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(a)u,u\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^{2d}}a(x,\xi)W_\epsilon[u](x,\xi)\,dx\,d\xi , $$

$$ \int_{\mathbb R^d}W_\epsilon[u](x,\xi)\,d\xi=|u(x)|^2,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R^d}W_\epsilon[u](x,\xi)\,dx=|(\mathcal F_\epsilon u)(\xi)|^2. $$

The Wigner distribution need not be nonnegative.

items.title: Order-zero Weyl L² boundedness
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\geq1$, $0<\epsilon\leq1$, and set $N_d=4d+4$. For a smooth $a:\mathbb R^{2d}\to\mathbb C$ with $\partial^\alpha a$ bounded for every $|\alpha|\leq N_d$, define

$$ \mathcal W_\epsilon[u,v](x,\xi):=(2\pi\epsilon)^{-d}\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-iy\cdot\xi/\epsilon}u(x+y/2)\overline{v(x-y/2)}\,dy $$

for $u,v\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, and define the Weyl operator initially as the form

$$ B_{\epsilon,a}(u,v):=\int_{\mathbb R^{2d}}a(x,\xi)\mathcal W_\epsilon[u,v](x,\xi)\,dx\,d\xi . $$

There is a unique bounded operator $\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(a)$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$ representing this form, and

$$ \|\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(a)\|_{L^2\to L^2}\leq C_d\sum_{|\alpha|\leq N_d}\|\partial^\alpha a\|_\infty , $$

where $C_d$ depends only on $d$. For $a\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{2d})$, this extension agrees with the kernel definition in [def-nrqmx-weyl-symbol-wigner].

items.title: Weyl composition with a controlled Schwartz remainder
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\geq1$, $0<\epsilon\leq1$, and $a,b\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{2d})$. Use the Poisson bracket

$$ \{a,b\}(x,\xi):=\nabla_xa(x,\xi)\cdot\nabla_\xi b(x,\xi)-\nabla_\xi a(x,\xi)\cdot\nabla_xb(x,\xi). $$

There is $r_\epsilon\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{2d})$ such that

$$ \operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(a)\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(b) =\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon\!\left(ab+\frac{i\epsilon}{2}\{a,b\}\right) +\epsilon^2\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(r_\epsilon). $$

There is an integer $M_d=12d+16$ and a constant $C_d$, independent of $\epsilon$, such that

$$ \|\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(r_\epsilon)\|_{L^2\to L^2} \leq C_d\,p_{M_d}(a)p_{M_d}(b),\qquad p_M(f):=\max_{|\alpha|\leq M}\sup_z\langle z\rangle^M|\partial^\alpha f(z)|,\quad \langle z\rangle:=(1+|z|^2)^{1/2}. $$

items.title: Cubic Weyl commutator remainder for a smooth potential
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\geq1$, $0<\epsilon\leq1$, and let $V\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R)$ have every partial derivative of total order at least $2$ bounded. Put

$$ h(x,\xi):=\frac{|\xi|^2}{2}+V(x),\qquad H_\epsilon^0:=-\frac{\epsilon^2}{2}\Delta+V(x)\quad\hbox{on }\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d). $$

For $a\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{2d})$, define $\{a,h\}=\nabla_xa\cdot\nabla_\xi h-\nabla_\xi a\cdot\nabla_xh$. There is a smooth symbol $r_{\epsilon,a,V}$ whose derivatives through order $N_d=4d+4$ are bounded uniformly for $0<\epsilon\leq1$, and on $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$

$$ \frac{i}{\epsilon}[H_\epsilon^0,\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(a)] =\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(\{a,h\})+\epsilon^2\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(r_{\epsilon,a,V}). $$

The last operator is the bounded-symbol extension of [lem-nrqmx-bounded-symbol-estimate]; for $M_d=12d+16$,

$$ \sum_{|\alpha|\leq N_d}\|\partial^\alpha r_{\epsilon,a,V}\|_\infty \leq C_{d,V}p_{M_d}(a),\qquad p_M(f):=\max_{|\beta|\leq M}\sup_z\langle z\rangle^M|\partial^\beta f(z)|,\quad \langle z\rangle=(1+|z|^2)^{1/2}. $$

items.title: Fixed-time Weyl Egorov estimate for subquadratic potentials
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $0<\epsilon\le1$, and $V\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R)$ with every partial derivative of total order at least $2$ bounded. Set
$$ h(x,\xi)=\frac{|\xi|^2}{2}+V(x),\qquad H_\epsilon^0=-\frac{\epsilon^2}{2}\Delta+V(x)\quad\text{on }\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d). $$
Assume, as an explicit operator hypothesis, that for each $\epsilon$ a densely defined self-adjoint operator $H_\epsilon$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$ extends $H_\epsilon^0$ and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ is a core for $H_\epsilon$. Let $U_\epsilon(t)$, $t\in\mathbb R$, be the strongly continuous unitary group with $U_\epsilon(0)=I$, preserving $D(H_\epsilon)$ and satisfying
$$ i\,\partial_tU_\epsilon(t)y=\epsilon^{-1}H_\epsilon U_\epsilon(t)y\qquad(y\in D(H_\epsilon)). $$
Thus its generator is $-iH_\epsilon/\epsilon$; for $t<0$, $U_\epsilon(t)=U_\epsilon(-t)^*$. Define the global Hamiltonian flow by
$$ \dot x=\xi,\qquad \dot\xi=-\nabla V(x),\qquad \Phi_0=I. $$
For every $a\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{2d})$ and finite $T>0$, there is $C_{T,V,a}<\infty$, independent of $0<\epsilon\le1$, such that
$$ \sup_{|t|\le T} \left\|U_\epsilon(t)^*\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(a)U_\epsilon(t) -\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(a\circ\Phi_t)\right\|_{L^2\to L^2} \le C_{T,V,a}\epsilon^2. $$
Only fixed finite times are covered by the first estimate. No Ehrenfest-time, caustic-uniformity, or physical measurement conclusion is asserted. If $V$ is a polynomial of degree at most two, the difference in that branch is identically zero.

There is also an exact statement for every real quadratic phase-space Hamiltonian. Let $z=(x,\xi)\in\mathbb R^{2d}$, let $G=G^T\in\mathbb R^{2d\times2d}$, $\ell\in\mathbb R^{2d}$ and $c\in\mathbb R$, and put
$$ h(z)=\tfrac12 z^TGz+\ell\cdot z+c. $$
Set $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_d\\-I_d&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $\widehat z=(Q_1,\ldots,Q_d,P_1,\ldots,P_d)$, where $Q_j u=x_j u$ and $P_j u=-i\epsilon\partial_{x_j}u$ on $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$. On $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ define the Weyl realization by
$$ H_{\epsilon,h}^0:=cI+\sum_j\ell_j\widehat z_j+\tfrac14\sum_{j,k}G_{jk}(\widehat z_j\widehat z_k+\widehat z_k\widehat z_j). $$
For each $0<\epsilon\le1$, assume a densely defined self-adjoint operator $H_{\epsilon,h}$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$ extends $H_{\epsilon,h}^0$ and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ is a core for it. Let $U_{\epsilon,h}(t)$ be the strongly continuous unitary group with $U_{\epsilon,h}(0)=I$, preserving $D(H_{\epsilon,h})$ and satisfying
$$ i\,\partial_tU_{\epsilon,h}(t)y=\epsilon^{-1}H_{\epsilon,h}U_{\epsilon,h}(t)y\qquad(y\in D(H_{\epsilon,h})). $$
Its generator is $-iH_{\epsilon,h}/\epsilon$. The global Hamiltonian flow, defined by $\dot z=J\nabla h(z)=J(Gz+\ell)$ and $\Phi_0(z)=z$, is
$$ \Phi_t(z)=e^{tJG}z+\int_0^t e^{(t-s)JG}J\ell\,ds. $$
Here $e^{tJG}:=\sum_{n=0}^\infty t^n(JG)^n/n!$ is the matrix exponential.
Then for every $a\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{2d})$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$ U_{\epsilon,h}(t)^*\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(a)U_{\epsilon,h}(t)=\operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(a\circ\Phi_t). $$

title: Weyl quantization, Wigner functions and finite-time classical limits — Examples

items.title: Exact harmonic-oscillator transport of a Gaussian Wigner density
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, let $0<\epsilon\le1$, and use the one-dimensional oscillator
$$ H_\epsilon=-\frac{\epsilon^2}{2}\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+\frac{x^2}{2} $$
with its self-adjoint oscillator realization. For real $q,p$, the normalized Gaussian
$$ \psi^\epsilon_{q,p}(x)=(\pi\epsilon)^{-1/4} \exp\!\left(-\frac{(x-q)^2}{2\epsilon}\right) \exp\!\left(\frac{ip(x-q/2)}{\epsilon}\right) $$
has Wigner density
$$ W_\epsilon[\psi^\epsilon_{q,p}](x,\xi)= \frac1{\pi\epsilon}\exp\!\left(-\frac{(x-q)^2+(\xi-p)^2}{\epsilon}\right). $$
Write $z=(z_1,z_2)=(x,\xi)$. For a measurable density $\rho:\mathbb R^2\to[0,\infty)$ with $\int\rho=1$ and $\int(|z|+|z|^2)\rho(z)\,dz<\infty$, define its mean and covariance by
$$ \mu_j(\rho):=\int_{\mathbb R^2}z_j\rho(z)\,dz,\qquad \Sigma_{jk}(\rho):=\int_{\mathbb R^2}(z_j-\mu_j(\rho))(z_k-\mu_k(\rho))\rho(z)\,dz. $$
This Wigner density has mean $(q,p)$ and covariance $(\epsilon/2)I_2$. On $\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$ let $Qf(x)=xf(x)$ and $Pf(x)=-i\epsilon f'(x)$. For a normalized $\varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$, define $\bar Q_\varphi=\langle Q\varphi,\varphi\rangle$, $\bar P_\varphi=\langle P\varphi,\varphi\rangle$, $\Delta_\varphi Q=\|(Q-\bar Q_\varphi)\varphi\|_2$, and $\Delta_\varphi P=\|(P-\bar P_\varphi)\varphi\|_2$. These standard deviations satisfy $\Delta_\varphi Q\,\Delta_\varphi P\ge\epsilon/2$, and the displayed Gaussian attains equality with both deviations $\sqrt{\epsilon/2}$.
Let $U_\epsilon(t)=e^{-itH_\epsilon/\epsilon}$, and define the evolved state's distributional Wigner functional on $a\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ by
$$ \langle W_t,a\rangle:=\langle \operatorname{Op}^W_\epsilon(a)U_\epsilon(t)\psi^\epsilon_{q,p}, U_\epsilon(t)\psi^\epsilon_{q,p}\rangle . $$
Then it is represented by the exact density
$$ W_t(x,\xi)=\frac1{\pi\epsilon} \exp\!\left(-\frac{(x-q_t)^2+(\xi-p_t)^2}{\epsilon}\right), \quad q_t=q\cos t+p\sin t,\quad p_t=p\cos t-q\sin t. $$
Thus this quadratic model transports the Gaussian Wigner density exactly along its classical Hamiltonian flow; its phase-space mean follows $(q_t,p_t)$ and its covariance remains $(\epsilon/2)I_2$. This is a mathematical model calculation, not an experimental observation.

items.title: A first excited oscillator state has negative Wigner values
items.statement:
The assertion to be refuted is: for every $0<\epsilon\le1$ and every normalized $u\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$, $W_\epsilon[u](x,\xi)\ge0$ for all $(x,\xi)\in\mathbb R^2$.

Assume Countable Choice and $0<\epsilon\le1$. In the one-dimensional oscillator with $m=\omega=1$, $\hbar=\epsilon$, the normalized first excited state is
$$ \psi^\epsilon_1(x)=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\epsilon}}(\pi\epsilon)^{-1/4} x\,e^{-x^2/(2\epsilon)}. $$
Its Wigner function is
$$ W_\epsilon[\psi^\epsilon_1](x,\xi) =\frac1{\pi\epsilon} \left(\frac{2(x^2+\xi^2)}{\epsilon}-1\right) e^{-(x^2+\xi^2)/\epsilon}. $$
It is strictly negative on the disk $x^2+\xi^2<\epsilon/2$. Consequently the assertion that every normalized Schwartz vector has a nonnegative Wigner function is false.
